title: Accounts Receivable Basis: Payment of Invoices Raised under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement
content:
Catering invoices fall due the number of days after the invoice date printed against the service level, and a payment is recorded against the single invoice it settles.

**Which agreements take a payment.** A payment is accepted on an agreement that stands active, on credit hold or closed, because a client settling arrears is exactly how a hold is lifted and a closed agreement may still carry a balance. The state the agreement stands in and its unsettled balance are read from the company's own agreement record before the payment is recorded.

**What clearing the balance does.** A payment that clears the whole unsettled balance on an agreement standing on credit hold is the trigger for the hold to be reviewed, and ordering reopens once the review is done rather than automatically on receipt.

**Part payments and overpayments.** A part payment settles the named invoice in part and never spills onto another invoice; an overpayment leaves the excess on the agreement to be applied to the next invoice raised.

**Late charges.** A late charge is the monthly late percentage printed against the service level applied to the amount still outstanding once the grace days printed against the same service level have passed, held to the late charge ceiling printed against that service level.

**Disputes.** Where an invoice is disputed in writing before the grace days expire, no late charge is raised while the dispute stands open, and the due date is not moved.

| Agreement stands as | A payment is accepted |
| --- | --- |
| Active | yes |
| On credit hold | yes |
| Closed | yes |
| Pending credit review | no |

### Illustration

Take a hypothetical Corporate Catering Service Agreement carrying two unsettled invoices. A payment tendered against the first settles that invoice alone; where it exceeds what the first invoice asks, the excess stays on the agreement for the next invoice raised and does not settle the second. Where it falls short, the first invoice stands part settled and the second is untouched.
